item.title: BMG Buys Andrew Stockdale’s Wolfmother Rights
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to Trending on Billboard! Today, we're talking about a major acquisition in the music industry. BMG has just acquired a significant chunk of rights related to Andrew Stockdale's interests in the Grammy Award-winning Australian rock band, Wolfmother.
[Short music transition]
Host: The deal includes control over Stockdale's publishing, recorded music royalties, and neighboring rights interests for Wolfmother's entire catalog. This extends a decade-long partnership between BMG and Stockdale, which began in 2016 when BMG became his global publisher.
[Short music transition]
Host: Heath Johns, President of BMG in Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, has a long history with Stockdale, having signed him to his first publishing deal back in 2005. Johns comments, "Few Australian bands have built a catalog with the global reach, cultural impact, and enduring influence of Wolfmother."
[Short music clip from Wolfmother]
Host: Wolfmother burst onto the scene with their self-titled album in 2005, featuring hit songs like "Woman", "Joker And The Thief", and "White Unicorn". They've since gone on to win multiple ARIA Awards, a Grammy, and have had their music featured in major films, TV shows, and video games, including The Hangover, Jackass Number Two, and Guitar Hero.
[Short music transition]
Host: Stockdale himself is thrilled about the deal, saying, "I couldn't think of a better place to have my share of the catalog than BMG." He praises Heath Johns and the team at BMG for their enthusiasm and expertise in helping cement Wolfmother's music in popular culture.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode of Trending on Billboard. Thanks for tuning in! We'll be back with more music industry news and updates soon.
